title: Release Pulse: weekly slice gating, RC fencing, and automated release notes
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our weekly release train currently exposes surface area where late regressions slip into RCs because the gating window is coarse and release notes are manually assembled. That creates churn in Dedicated/Private upgrade lanes and makes LTS promotion risky.

Goal: Build a Release Pulse system that slices weekly builds into short gating windows, enforces an RC "fence" (golden-rc-lock) to prevent late risky merges, and generates consistent, diff-driven release notes automatically. Enable safer LTS promotions by attaching automated stability heuristics to RC candidates.

Scope:
- Implement 'slice windows' for weekly builds so we produce 3 short candidate slices per week (alpha/beta/rc-pre) and a single weekly RC cut.
- RC fencing: automated guard that prevents merges into the RC branch after cut except via an explicit hotfix flow with approvals.
- Release notes automation: ingest changelogs from merged PRs, highlight breaking changes, link regression test failures, and auto-generate notes in Markdown suitable for the Console changelog and GitHub release.
- Integrate with existing dashboards to surface per-slice failure rates and quantile latency regressions used for gating decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Weekly pipeline produces named slices (alpha, beta, rc-pre, rc) and publishes artifacts to staging storage.
RC fence prevents direct merges into rc/* branches; hotfix flow requires two approvers or a security bypass with audit log.
Automated release notes script (release-pulse/generate) produces a Markdown file containing PR summaries, linked issues, breaking changes, and per-test-suite failure trends.
Dashboard shows slice-level pass/fail and latency p50/p95 deltas; gating alerts fire when stability heuristics cross thresholds.
Canary promotion to LTS must be backed by at least 3 stable RCs over 2 weeks OR explicit PM sign-off with documented mitigations.
implementation_plan: Design slice naming and schedule: allocate Monday/Wednesday/Friday short slices; finalize cut windows with SRE team.
Add pipeline job 'build-slice' that runs model compile, smoke tests, and artifact publish; artifacts tagged with slice name and hash.
Implement 'rc-fence' GitHub Action that rejects merges to rc/* unless commit contains HOTFIX token and PR has required approvals.
Build 'notes-generator' Lambda that queries merged PRs by tag range, extracts structured notes, and runs heuristics for breaking-change detection.
Wire metrics: publish slice-level test pass rates and latency quantiles to Console; add gating rule evaluator to release-train service.
risks: Tight slice windows could overload CI if flaky tests are not reduced; need to flip a subset of tests to 'slice-fast' mode.
Automated note heuristics may miss contextual product impact (false negatives); require a manual review step for high-impact changes.
RC fence combined with emergency hotfix flow could introduce human bottlenecks if approvers are unavailable; define fallback on-call rotation.
test_plan: Unit tests for notes-generator extraction heuristics with curated PR samples (including multi-commit feature PRs).
Integration test for rc-fence action simulating merges and HOTFIX flows in a test repo.
End-to-end trial run for one week: produce slices, allow two-week observation window for stability metrics, and validate automated release notes against manual notes.

2025-03-06 - PM review (Jon Wu): Agreed on conservative default gating thresholds; asked for ability to override with PM sign-off for customer hotfixes.
2025-03-07 - Design (Marta Ruiz): Provided changelog template variants for Console and GitHub release pages, emphasized breaking-change callout needs to surface in Console.

notes: Trade-offs discussed: conservative fence reduces churn but may delay urgent patches; proposed solution is an explicit HOTFIX token plus 2 approvers or on-call override with audit.
Follow-ups: migrate existing 'weekly-cut' jobs to slice-aware variants (ENG-40900) and add audit logging for any fence bypass (ENG-41250).
Post-deployment: run two trial weeks and capture false-positive/negative rates of note heuristics; iterate with a small scoreboard.
